title: Privacy Policy | Crenosoft
desc: How Crenosoft collects, uses, stores and discloses personal information through our website, AI assistant and AI services, under the Privacy Act 1988.
lead: This policy explains how Crenosoft handles personal information, including information collected through our website, our AI assistant and the AI services we provide to clients.
body:
Who we are

In this policy, “Crenosoft”, “we”, “us” and “our” means [Australian entity name], ABN [ABN], of [street address], Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, together with our related entities that help us deliver our services. We are committed to handling personal information in line with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs).

You can contact our privacy officer at [privacy email] or by post at the address above.

What personal information we collect

  • Contact details such as your name, business name, role, email address and phone number when you complete a form, book an audit or contact us.
  • Enquiry content, such as what you would like to automate and any information you choose to include in a message.
  • AI assistant and tool inputs, such as questions you type into our website chat, tasks you describe to our live AI agent and answers you give in our AI readiness check.
  • Service information when you become a client, such as billing details, contract records and communications with our team.
  • Technical information, such as your IP address, browser type and the pages you visit, collected automatically by our hosting provider and web services.

We do not intentionally collect sensitive information through our website. Please do not enter health information or other sensitive details into our forms, chat or AI tools.

How we collect personal information

We collect personal information directly from you when you use our website, contact us, attend a meeting or become a client. We may also collect business contact information from public sources such as company websites and professional networks. If we receive information we did not ask for, we will decide whether we could have collected it lawfully and, if not, destroy or de-identify it where reasonable.

How we use personal information

  • to respond to your enquiry and arrange your free AI audit
  • to provide, operate, support and improve our services
  • to generate responses from our website AI assistant and AI tools
  • to send service updates and, where you have asked to receive them, information about our services
  • to manage billing, contracts and our business records
  • to comply with our legal obligations and protect our rights

You can opt out of marketing communications at any time using the unsubscribe link or by contacting us.

Our website AI assistant and AI tools

Our website includes an AI assistant, a live automation demo and an AI readiness check. When you use them, the text you enter is sent to a third-party AI model provider to generate a response. These features are for general information only. Please do not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into them. We configure our AI providers so that, where the provider offers this option, your inputs are not used to train public models. See our AI Policy for more about how we use AI responsibly.

Information we process for our clients

When we build and run AI systems for clients, such as AI receptionists, chatbots or document processing, we handle personal information about our clients’ customers on our clients’ behalf. In those cases we act as our client’s service provider and handle that information according to our agreement with the client and the client’s own privacy obligations. If you are a customer of one of our clients, please contact that business about its privacy practices.

Who we disclose personal information to

We disclose personal information only as needed to run our business and deliver our services, including to:

  • our staff and related entities who help deliver our services
  • hosting, cloud and website providers
  • AI model providers that power our assistant, tools and client systems
  • email, CRM, scheduling, telephony and payment providers
  • professional advisers such as accountants, auditors and lawyers
  • regulators, law enforcement or others where required or authorised by law

We do not sell personal information.

Overseas disclosure

Some of our service providers, including AI model and cloud providers, may store or process information outside Australia, including in the United States. Members of our team who deliver human review and engineering services may be located in India. Where we disclose personal information overseas, we take reasonable steps under APP 8 to ensure it is handled in line with the APPs, including contractual safeguards, confidentiality obligations, access controls and logging. Clients can request Australia-only handling for their services where their obligations require it.

Cookies and analytics

Our website uses only the technical storage needed for it to work. It loads fonts from Google Fonts, which means your browser connects to Google’s servers. If we introduce analytics or advertising cookies, we will update this policy before doing so.

How we protect personal information

We take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure. Measures include encrypted connections, access limited to people who need it, multi-factor authentication on key systems, logging and regular review of our providers. We keep personal information only for as long as we need it for the purposes above or as required by law, and then destroy or de-identify it.

If we experience a data breach likely to result in serious harm, we will assess it and notify affected individuals and the OAIC as required under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.

Accessing and correcting your information

You can ask for access to the personal information we hold about you, or ask us to correct it, by contacting our privacy officer. We will respond within a reasonable time, usually 30 days. If we refuse a request, we will tell you why and how to complain.

Complaints

If you have a concern about how we have handled your personal information, please contact our privacy officer first and we will try to resolve it within 30 days. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC).

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The current version will always be on this page, with the date it was last updated.
